doc.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: His own records and career today
title: The session business today
summary: He says there are far more musicians than work now.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Before we get to — we have to talk about your own solo recordings. What has happened to the business? I think of all the jazz graduates coming out of the schools every year and many of them must head to L.A. Is there any — what’s the business like for them to head to these days?

Not great. Not great. I would put it to you this way: there is far more qualified musicians than there is work to keep them busy. And that’s a problem, a problem we didn’t have back then. But we have it now. The sessions are few and far between as we’ve gone to much computer-generated music and you know the advent of music that’s basically free off the Internet, or purchasable for a pittance. There’s no interest in doing a record for profit. It’s just not profitable anymore. So you know it’s just the opportunities just aren’t out there.
